Optimal.Notes: Locking to 40 fps at 40 Hz gives a smooth, tear-free experience with a reasonable battery life. Textures are kept on High to preserve the game's visual storytelling; shadows and vegetation are the biggest GPU costs and are dialed to Medium.

profiles.Summary: Kingdom Come: Deliverance is a demanding open-world RPG that runs on the Steam Deck with some effort — the GPU sits between the minimum and recommended specs, so expect 30–40 fps at low-to-medium settings with FSR upscaling. The game is rated Playable (not Verified) and ProtonDB reporters trend platinum, suggesting it works well under Proton with minor tweaks.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs relative to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class) and the ProtonDB gold/platinum trend. On your first run, check frame pacing in Rattay (the busiest town) and drop to the Optimal or Max Battery profile if you see sustained dips below 30 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 keeps the GPU load low enough for 8 W TDP. Towns will dip toward 28 fps; wilderness and interiors hold closer to 35.

KnownIssues: Small text in menus and dialogue can be hard to read on the 7-inch screen
Loading times can be long without an NVMe SSD — the Deck's internal storage helps but expect waits
Occasional stuttering in dense areas like towns (Rattay, Skalitz) due to CPU streaming
The game may require accepting the EULA and logging into a launcher on first launch, which can be awkward with a controller

MaxPerformance.Notes: Uncapping TDP lets the APU boost freely for the best frame rates; expect drops into the low 40s in Rattay and other dense towns. A 50 fps cap prevents the worst thermal spikes while staying well above 40.

Optimal.Notes: Running at 40 Hz with a 40 fps cap on the OLED panel delivers a notably smoother feel than 30 fps; FSR from 1024x640 keeps image quality acceptable. Expect the frame cap to hold in wilderness and light indoor areas, with occasional dips to ~35 fps in Rattay.

profiles.Summary: Kingdom Come: Deliverance is a demanding open-world RPG that runs on the Steam Deck at playable but modest frame rates; the CryEngine-based game is CPU and GPU intensive, especially in towns and dense forests. With reduced settings and FSR upscaling it can hold a stable 30 fps, though expect dips in the most demanding outdoor areas.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs (GTX 660 min, GTX 1060 recommended) compared to the Deck's ~GTX 1050 Ti class GPU, and the game's known CryEngine demands. On first run, check frame rates in Rattay (the most demanding town) and adjust settings or the TDP cap accordingly.

MaxBattery.Notes: Dropping render resolution to 960x600 with FSR upscaling and capping TDP at 8 W gives the longest session life. Towns will still dip to ~25 fps occasionally — accept this or lower Shadow Quality further.

KnownIssues: Towns and densely populated areas (Rattay, Sasau) can cause significant frame drops even at low settings
Long shader compilation stutters may occur on first launch or entering new areas
Some UI elements and subtitles may render small at 800p — check Accessibility options
Occasional Proton-related audio glitches reported; switching to Proton Experimental or GE-Proton may help

MaxPerformance.Notes: Removing TDP and GPU clock limits lets the APU boost freely for the best frame rates the Deck can sustain; 45 Hz cap smooths out variance. Battery drain will be high — this profile is best for docked or short sessions.
